text:
Predicates:
TwinOrTriplet(x) ::: x is a twin or triplet.
SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x, y) ::: x and y are siblings of the same age.
ComplainsAboutSibling(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LivesAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopsStrongFamilyBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with family members.
Premises:
∀x (TwinOrTriplet(x) → SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If a person is a twin or triplet, then he spends a lot of time with siblings.
∀x ∀y ((SameAgeSiblings(x, y)) → TwinOrTriplet(x) ∨ Triplet(x)) ::: If a person has siblings of the same age, then he is a twin or triplet.
∀x (ComplainsAboutSibling(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x, y)) ::: If a person complains often about siblings, then he has siblings of the same age.
∀x (¬LivesAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopsStrongFamilyBonds(x)) ::: If a person does not live at home regularly, then he does not develop strong family bonds.
∀x (SpendsTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LivesAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If a person spends a lot of time with siblings, then he does not live at home regularly.
Conclusion:
(TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ DevelopsStrongFamilyBonds(luke)) ∨ (¬TwinOrTriplet(luke) ∧ ¬DevelopsStrongFamilyBonds(luke)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family, or neither.
